title: This Bird Has No Body Heat for Its Eggs, So It Builds an Oven
subject: malleefowl

scenes.text: This bird can't warm its eggs. So it builds an oven.
The malleefowl, in Australia, piles sand and leaves into a mound a meter high and four meters across.
Rotting leaves inside make the heat. The male has to hold the eggs at 33 degrees Celsius.
To check, he pushes his bill into the mound like a thermometer. Too hot, he opens it to cool morning air.
Too cool, he lets in the afternoon sun. He does this through the whole breeding season.
Chicks dig for up to fifteen hours to reach the surface. Then they walk off alone. A day later, they can fly.

description:
The malleefowl doesn't sit on its eggs. It builds a compost oven instead.
The male keeps a mound of sand and rotting leaves at about 33 degrees Celsius, testing it with his bill and opening or covering it to heat or cool it. Chicks dig out alone, and can fly within a day.
Would you have the patience to run an oven all season?
first_comment: A bird that runs a thermometer and a compost oven, and then abandons its kids on day one. Would you want that dad?
